response.rationale: The confirmed pancreatic head adenocarcinoma with obstructive jaundice (F01, F05, F07, F09) and the severe myositis with CK >40,000 (F06) and MRI findings (F08) strongly support a paraneoplastic myositis/rhabdomyolysis, leading to acute kidney injury (F12). Statin-induced myopathy (D2) is possible but less likely given the acute presentation and cancer. Cholangiocarcinoma (D3) is less likely due to the pancreatic head mass. Obstructive uropathy (D4) is contradicted by the high CK. Polymyositis (D5) is unlikely given no autoimmune history. The temporal and clinical context favor D1.
